cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Raise the Impossibility
cards.instruction: Answer every strange offer with a more committed version that you can still justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your venue accepts invisible wedding guests? Reserve places for their families too; nobody arrives to find themselves uncounted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The families walk through walls. We offer a ballroom that follows them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll book it with tables that keep pace. Guests shouldn't have to chase their dinner; please include that in the price.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The ballroom can split when guests wander in different directions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then add a cake that multiplies with it. One cutting time for every room, please; we won't make anyone watch the others get served first.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects table movement and A5 synchronized service, committing to additional impossible hospitality after each venue offer.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 following ballroom causes A3 matching tables; B4 splitting rooms causes A5 multiplying cake and shared cutting time.

relationship.evidence: B2/B4 explain venue capabilities to a buyer, a coherent supplier role from A1 onward.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 divided guests to require equal simultaneous service rather than a detachable bigger miracle.

specificity.evidence: A1 venue and wedding guests establish roles; B2/B4 moving and splitting behavior is explicitly offered.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 equality rationale explains the order to the supplier; it is a little long but all parts concern the same service requirement.
